questions.title: What are Enums commonly referred to as in type theory?
questions.explanation: Enums are sum types (or tagged unions) because an instance holds one (and only one) of its possible variants at any given time.

questions.title: What is the default visibility of fields (associated data) within enum variants?
options: Their visibility matches the module visibility
You must explicitly add `pub` before each variant field
questions.explanation: Unlike struct fields, fields and payload data within enum variants in Rust are automatically public.

questions.title: Which variant in `enum Foo { A, B(u32), C { val: bool } }` is a struct-like variant?
questions.explanation: Variant `C` with named fields enclosed in curly braces `{}` is a struct variant, behaving similarly to a traditional struct.

questions.title: What constitutes an uninhabited type when declared as an enum?
options: An enum where all variants are marked as deprecated
An enum that contains zero variants
An enum containing only empty unit variants
questions.explanation: An enum declared without any variants (e.g. `enum Empty {}`) is an uninhabited type because it is impossible to create an instance of it.

questions.title: How do you safely extract associated data from an enum variant?
options: Using pattern matching (e.g., via `match` or `if let`)
Using dot notation to access the variant index (e.g., `event.KeyPress.0`)
By binding the data to a global variable
questions.explanation: The only safe way to access data stored in enum variants in Rust is by testing which variant is currently active through pattern matching.
